summary.value: The Catalana, also called the Catalana del Prat, was bred near Barcelona in Catalonia, Spain, during the late 1800s from local farm hens crossed with Asian birds. It was shown to the world at the 1902 fair in Madrid and joined the American standard in 1949. Birds are a rich buff to reddish gold with black tails that shine green, white earlobes and slate blue legs. Roosters weigh about 8 pounds and hens about 6. Hens lay roughly 200 to 240 white to pale pink eggs a year, medium to large in size, and seldom go broody. The meat is also well regarded, so it serves as a dual purpose bird. Catalanas are alert, active and wary of people, fly readily and dislike being penned. They handle extreme heat very well, which makes them a strong pick for hot climates.
